content:
marco: heads up — support escalated a customer on dedicated who is seeing p95/p99 regressions since last night's runtime deploy. they report tail latency doubled for short-seq chat (<=128).

jen: ack, any evidence it's our rollout?

marco: yes — correlates with canary that flipped kernel selection heuristics to prefer FlashAttention (FA) for compat_v2 models. deploy-bot shows rollout at 2123412000 -> commit `a7c9f1d`. support-bot pasted customer traces.

support-bot: Customer traces (redacted): request ids [req-7a2, req-7a3, req-7a4], sample latencies: p50 45ms, p95 210ms (was ~95ms), p99 480ms (was ~220ms).

alex: interesting — FA normally faster for long seqs but can be worse for short sequences on certain GPU kernels and with SDPA emulation. did we also change compile flags?

rachel: yes, CI shows change in build flags in that commit: `-DUSE_FLASHATTN=1 -DUSE_SDPA=1 -O3 -march=native`. additionally kernel selector switched to `prefer_flash_attn=true` when memory/seq heuristics matched.

mike: I ran a quick perf on a repro VM using the customer's prompt length. For 64 and 128 tokens FA kernel shows more kernel launch overhead and worse occupancy on A10g in their Dedicated pool. SDPA path has extra memcpy and fallback scalar path for short heads. logs: 
```
trace: kernel_launch_time: 0.48ms -> 1.2ms
trace: aten_flash_attn_forward: 0.82ms -> 2.5ms
cache: kv_cache_misses increased by 12% at p99
```

marco: repro steps (local inference harness):
```
# reproduce locally against the canary runtime image
git checkout a7c9f1d
python -m rwinference.bench --model compat_v2/13b --gpu A10g --seq 128 --batch 1 --measure p99 --samples 500
```

marco: also repro via curl to customer's Dedicated endpoint (redacted):
```
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"input":"<short prompt>", "max_tokens":128}' https://dedicated.rwinf.internal/v1/generate?model=compat_v2-13b
```

jen: immediate mitigations we can flip: 1) toggle fallback to SDPA-less legacy kernels, 2) force `REDWOOD_USE_FLASHATTN=false` in canary routing, 3) revert kernel selector change. what's fastest?

alex: fastest is env toggle on gateway for affected pool (no rebuild). add logic: prefer `kernel_version=legacy` or set REDWOOD_USE_FLASHATTN=0. I can push override to the canary config in 5 min.

rachel: we should also push a patch to kernel selector to add seq-length threshold for FA (e.g., only enable FA for seq >= 256 or head_count >= 32). that's the root fix.

luis: can we A/B route only high-latency customers to legacy until fixed? we have per-customer routing rules.

marco: yes. customer asked for quick fix. mike can you confirm toggling env will bring p95 back?

mike: I applied a local env override and re-ran bench: p95 went from 210ms -> 92ms, p99 480ms -> 215ms. So yes.

jen: go for it. alex, push the override and add a temporary flag in control plane. include audit annotation.

alex: pushing config now. will tag change `hotfix/disable-fa-2123456789`. deploy-bot: starting rollout to dedicated pool `dedicated-eu-3`...

deploy-bot: rollout 2123457890 started for config hotfix/disable-fa-2123456789 -> target: dedicated-eu-3 (10 nodes)

marco: action items:
- alex: hotfix rollout + add per-pool override (in progress)
- rachel: patch kernel selector + add unit tests for seq thresholds (PR target EOD)
- mike: run regression sweep across GPU types (A10g, A100s, H100) and shader versions, collect p50/p95/p99
- jen: notify customer and offer temporary routing to legacy kernels, include expected resolution ETA
- luis: if customer says OK, add permanent route until release cut

rachel: quick note — observed CPU-side compile flag `-march=native` led to different vectorization on our build host vs dedicated nodes; we should normalize build flags across artifact matrix. Added to PR too.

mike: also found that when batching enabled `--batch_timeout_ms` small (we set 8ms) batching reduces kernel inefficiency; for single-request low-latency flow batching hurts. Might add dynamic batch timeout per kernel.

marco: summarizing timeline for customer: hotfix rolled at 2123457890, validation showed p95 recovered. customer-facing message drafted below.

jen: paste suggested note to customer please.

marco: suggested message:
"We identified a regression introduced by a kernel selection change in last night's rollout that caused FlashAttention to be used for short-sequence workloads on some GPUs. We've applied a configuration hotfix to route your traffic to the legacy kernel path which restores p95/p99 to previous levels. Our engineering team is working on a permanent fix (selector thresholds + build normalization) and we'll follow up with a patch timeline. Sorry for the disruption and thanks for the report."

support-bot: Customer acknowledged and accepted temporary routing.

alex: hotfix rollout completed at 2123458000. monitoring shows p95 for that customer's pool back to baseline.

deploy-bot: rollout 2123457890 completed -> dedicated-eu-3

mike: running cross-GPU sweep now, early notes: H100 sees less regression (FA optimized), A10g and A100 gen1 show biggest wins from legacy path for short seq. Will upload full matrix to the incident doc.

rachel: created PR #4123 with kernel selector thresholds and fixed compile flags. request review from runtime owners.

marco: great. please update this thread with links to the perf matrix and the PR. once PR merges we'll schedule a gradual canary with stronger telemetry for seq-length vs kernel mapping.

luis: nits — add a metric for `kernel.choice` in per-request tracing (value=flashattn|legacy|sdpa-fallback) so we can roll forward safely.

jen: agreed. add to telemetry backlog (priority P0 for this week).

marco: ok closing for now since hotfix restored customer SLAs. keep thread open for PR and perf artifacts. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
